sost.story: Traveller, Sost, Afghanistan, is a village in Badakhshan Province. Sost, Pakistan, is the last town inside Pakistan on the Karakoram Highway before the Chinese border. Sost, Hautes-Pyrénées, is a commune in France, and Söst is in Germany. These are the places the name Sost can mean.
sost.name: Sost

morkhun.story: Traveller, as you move along the Karakoram Highway in Gilgit-Baltistan, you’ll find the small village of Moorkhun beside the Hunza River, about 180 kilometres upriver from Gilgit and across a small river from Boibar valley. It is the eighth village from Gulmit towards the China–Pakistan border at the Khunjerab Pass and sits 5 kilometres before the Pakistani port of entry at Sust, surrounded by large mountains. This is the gateway to the old route to Shimshal village, where the trek from the Karakoram Highway follows the Boiber River through Avgarch village, Chilkhun, Boiber, Piryar and Dut pass, with forks to Qaroon Peak and Jurjur Khoon Sar peak. Locals say the name comes from Wakhi, spoken in Badakhshan and Pamir, where “Moor” means “rain” and “Khun” means “house”—roughly, “rain house.”
morkhun.name: Morkhoon

khunjerab-national-park.story: For a traveller, Khunjerab National Park in Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan, is Pakistan’s third largest national park and is adjacent to the Taxkorgan Natural Reserve in China. Its name comes from Wakhi, the native language of the region, where Khun means “blood” and jerav means “to stream.” The park was established primarily to protect the Marco Polo sheep, as well as snow leopards and bharal living in the area, and its borders were mapped by George Schaller of the Wildlife Conservation Society in 1974 after a short field survey. It was formally established on 29 April 1975 by Prime Minister of Pakistan Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who said that “it must become a world famous park.”
khunjerab-national-park.name: Khunjerab National Park

khunjerab-pass.story: Traveller, when you reach Khunjerab Pass, you are on a high-altitude mountain pass on the Karakoram Highway, in Pakistani-administered Gilgit-Baltistan bordering the Xinjiang Autonomous Region of China. At 4,693 metres above sea level in the Karakoram, it holds a strategic position on Pakistan’s northern border in the Hunza and Nagar districts and on China’s southwestern border with Pakistan. Its Wakhi name means “waterfall house,” from “Khun” for house and “Jerab” for a creek coming from a spring or a waterfall, while nearby Mutsjliga Pass stands at 5,314 metres. As the highest paved international border crossing globally and the highest point along the Karakoram Highway, it has, since the road across it was completed in 1982, supplanted the unpaved Mintaka and Kilik passes as the principal route across the Karakoram Range.
khunjerab-pass.name: Khunjerab Pass
